Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Shaquille O’Neal Calls Walker Kessler Best Big Man In NBA After Lakers Debut Lakers News Shaquille O’Neal Calls Walker Kessler Best Big Man In NBA After Lakers Debut
 Corey Hansford Published: 10/23/2026 3 Min Read Oct 21, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) reaches for the ball against Golden State Warriors center Al Horford (20) in the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images SHARE There was a lot of pressure on new Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler coming into his regular season debut. The Lakers traded a lot to acquire him from the Utah Jazz and the history of Lakers big men is immense with the likes of Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Shaquille O’Neal and Wilt Chamberlain having their jerseys hanging in the rafters.
 Thankfully, Kessler had a literal perfect debut as he made all 12 of his shots to finish with 26 points, nine rebounds and two blocks in the Lakers’ 127-105 win over the Golden State Warriors . It was as impressive a performance as anyone could imagine and one legend who was more impressed than anyone was O’Neal, who proclaimed Kessler to be the best big man in the league, via NBA on ESPN :
 "Walker Kessler is the best big man in the NBA."
 @SHAQ has high praise for the Lakers’ new center after his season debut 🙌 https://t.co/rhiECypFH9
 — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 22, 2026 
 This is probably a case of O’Neal going a bit overboard in his praise, as Nikola Jokic and Victor Wembanyama are still in the NBA. But O’Neal is also much more of a traditional big, just like Kessler, and thus he appreciates his style a bit more. And O’Neal continued that praise when Kessler joined the show later on that night:
 Shaq showed some major love to Walker Kessler after his #Lakers debut. https://t.co/ZsfhPdIlvx
 — Lakers Nation (@LakersNation) October 22, 2026 
 Kessler’s Lakers debut wasn’t just great, it was historical . He joined Wilt Chamberlain as the only Lakers to shoot perfect from the field with at least 12 shot attempts, and his 10 dunks were the most by any Lakers player since O’Neal back in 2003.
 As Kessler noted, getting that level of praise from someone like O’Neal who is not only a Lakers legend, but the most dominant force in NBA history in the eyes of most, just means that much more. It should only serve as extra motivation to continue playing at this level, but it will also come with increased expectations as now everyone has seen what he is capable of and he will need to deliver on a nightly basis.
 JJ Redick wants Walker Kessler to be ‘relentless’ this season
 Kessler is embracing all of the pressure and expectations that comes with playing for the Lakers and he and head coach JJ Redick had plenty of conversations prior to the start of the season about the big man being ‘relentless’ on both sides of the court every game .
